finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes an unvalidated, attacker-supplied query parameter directly to http.Get and streams the response back to the caller, enabling read-SSRF to loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; response body copied to client at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch route registered with no auth middleware
target read from query string with no parsing or validation
http.Get called on raw string; follows redirects by default
upstream response body streamed back to attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. Go's client rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes, which limits the reachable surface to HTTP(S) only.

verdict.guard_found: none. fetch() at main.go:14-23 has no validation between main.go:15 and the sink at main.go:16. The allowlist at main.go:9-12 and hostname check at main.go:27 are only in safeFetch, which is registered on /safe (main.go:42), not /fetch (main.go:41). The /fetch route has no auth middleware.
verdict.reason: main.go:15 takes the target query parameter unvalidated, main.go:16 passes it to http.Get (which follows redirects), and main.go:22 streams the response back to the caller, with no closing guard on the /fetch route at main.go:41. The candidate's trace is accurate.

finding.claim: The /safe handler checks only the first-hop hostname against an allowlist. http.Get follows redirects by default with no re-validation, so an allowlisted host that redirects to an internal address bypasses the check. Exploitability depends on an open redirect or attacker control on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which this code does not show.
finding.sink: http.Get(u.String()) at main.go:31; response body copied to client at main.go:37

trace.note: /safe route registered with no auth middleware
allowed[u.Hostname()] checked on the first hop only
http.Get follows up to 10 redirects with no per-hop check
redirected response body streamed back to attacker

finding.guards_checked: url.Parse and Hostname() on the same value that is fetched (blocks userinfo-@ tricks); exact-match map lookup (blocks case variants and trailing-dot hosts); scheme implicitly limited to HTTP(S) by Go's client. Redirect targets not checked.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the exact-match map lookup `allowed[u.Hostname()]` at main.go:27, which runs on the first hop only. No re-validation happens after the redirect at main.go:31. The /safe route is registered unauthenticated at main.go:42.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `target` query parameter (main.go:26) passes the first-hop allowlist check (main.go:27) and then reaches `http.Get` (main.go:31), which follows redirects by default with no per-hop check, and the response body is streamed back (main.go:37). Exploitation still requires an open redirect or attacker-controlled response on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which is not visible in this code, so the impact depends on that external condition.
